::: {.lead}
Today you take a small list from the first row to the last answer: clean
it, summarize it and chart it. Each experiment has two parts. **Part A**
is in Excel and an AI assistant on the lab computer. **Part B** is on a
simulator of the interactive lesson: on paper, scan its QR code; on the
screen, click its link. After each step, write your result in its box. At
the end, copy your key results into the table.
:::

## Before you start

- **You need:** a lab computer with Excel (the desktop app, or Excel on the
  web at `office.com`) and an AI assistant that the university allows (for
  example `copilot.microsoft.com` with your university account).
- **No lab computer today?** Do Part B of each experiment on your phone. Do
  Part A later on any computer with Excel.
- **Huda's list:** Huda keeps the store room of Sunrise Company. She wrote
  down the boxes of supplies that the staff took in three weeks, with **two
  mistakes**: the row *2, Cups, 2* was typed twice, and one item is
  *Glove* instead of *Gloves*. (The list is also on the interactive lesson,
  to copy.)

  | Week | Item   | Boxes |
  |:----:|--------|------:|
  | 1    | Paper  | 6     |
  | 1    | Gloves | 4     |
  | 2    | Paper  | 5     |
  | 2    | Glove  | 3     |
  | 2    | Cups   | 2     |
  | 2    | Cups   | 2     |
  | 3    | Paper  | 8     |
  | 3    | Gloves | 5     |
  | 3    | Cups   | 4     |

- **Check:** the results are at the end of this worksheet. Look only after
  you try. On the interactive lesson, every step has a check that answers
  at once.

## Experiment 1 · Clean the data and make a table

**The idea:** clean a list before you count it: one row for each record,
one kind of value in each column, no empty rows. Remove the **duplicate
rows** (**Data › Remove Duplicates**) and write each name the same way.
Then make the list an **Excel table** (**Ctrl + T**) and switch on its
**Total Row**.

**Aim:** clean Huda's list, and make it a table with a total.

::: {.part}
**Part A · In the app (Excel)**
:::

1. Type Huda's list into a new workbook, starting in cell **A1**, with its
   two mistakes. Click one cell of the list and choose **Data › Remove
   Duplicates** › OK.

   {{< record "Excel removed … ; rows left …" >}}

   ::: {.check}
   Excel removes **1 duplicate**, and **8 rows** stay: the cups of week 2
   now count once.
   :::

   ::: {.choice}
   Why do you remove a row that was typed twice?

   - [x] It counts twice in every total.

     Why: The same 2 boxes would be added two times.

   - [ ] It makes the list too long to print.

     Why: The problem is the wrong total, not the length.

   - [ ] Excel cannot sort a list with it.

     Why: Excel can sort it; the total is wrong.
   :::

2. Click the cell with *Glove* and type **Gloves**. Click one cell of the
   list › **Ctrl + T** › OK. Then choose **Table Design › Total Row**.

   {{< record "The total row shows …" >}}

   ::: {.check}
   **37 boxes** (6 + 4 + 5 + 3 + 2 + 8 + 5 + 4). With the row typed twice,
   the total was 39. The table also gets filter buttons and a name.
   :::

   ::: {.fill answer="37" unit="boxes" hint="Add the 8 clean rows: the cups of week 2 count once."}
   What does the total row show after cleaning?

   Why: 6 + 4 + 5 + 3 + 2 + 8 + 5 + 4 = 37 boxes. With the row typed twice, it was 39.
   :::

::: {.part}
**Part B · On the simulator** (no computer? do it on your phone)
:::

{{< sim file="../../week-07/sims/clean-data-lab.html" poster="../../week-07/sims/clean-data-lab.png" title="Clean Data Lab: tidy the sales list with AI advice" >}}

3. In **Clean Data Lab**, clean the list with the five good steps (skip the
   bad one). How many rows are left, and how many rows have the type
   *Drinks*?

   {{< record "Rows … ; Drinks …" >}}

   ::: {.check}
   **10 rows** and **4 drinks** (185 JD). Before cleaning, only 2 rows had
   the type *Drinks*: "drinks" and "drinks " (with a space) look different
   to Excel.
   :::

   ::: {.choice}
   Before cleaning, the lab counts only 2 rows with the type *Drinks*. Why?

   - [x] Some drinks are written "drinks" or "drinks ", with a space.

     Why: Write each name the same way, and TRIM the spaces.

   - [ ] Two drinks were deleted.

     Why: No row was deleted; the names are written in other ways.

   - [ ] The SUM is wrong.

     Why: The count of the type is wrong because of the spelling.
   :::

## Experiment 2 · Summarize with a PivotTable

**The idea:** **Insert › PivotTable**; one field in **Rows**, the number
field in **Values**. Change the rows to see the data from another side (by
item, by week). Check: the **Grand Total** must equal the total row of the
table.

**Aim:** summarize Huda's table by item and by week.

::: {.part}
**Part A · In the app (Excel)**
:::

1. Click one cell of the table › **Insert › PivotTable** › OK. Drag
   **Item** to **Rows** and **Boxes** to **Values**.

   {{< record "Paper … ; Gloves … ; Cups … ; Grand Total …" >}}

   ::: {.check}
   **Paper 19, Gloves 12, Cups 6; Grand Total 37**, the same as the total
   row. A row *Glove* means that the spelling was not fixed: fix it, then
   click **PivotTable Analyze › Refresh**.
   :::

   ::: {.choice}
   A PivotTable shows *Glove 3* and *Gloves 9*. What is wrong?

   - [x] One row has another spelling: fix it, then Refresh.

     Why: Excel sees two names, so it makes two rows.

   - [ ] Excel adds up wrong.

     Why: Excel adds right; the data has two names.

   - [ ] Glove is a new item.

     Why: It is the same item, written in another way.
   :::

2. Drag **Item** out of Rows, and drag **Week** into Rows.

   {{< record "Week 1 … ; week 2 … ; week 3 …" >}}

   ::: {.check}
   **10, 10 and 17 boxes**: week 3 took the most. The Grand Total is still
   37 boxes.
   :::

   ::: {.fill answer="17" unit="boxes" hint="Week 3: Paper 8, Gloves 5, Cups 4."}
   How many boxes did the staff take in week 3?

   Why: 8 + 5 + 4 = 17 boxes, the most of the three weeks.
   :::

::: {.part}
**Part B · On the simulator** (no computer? do it on your phone)
:::

{{< sim file="../../week-13/sims/pivot-lab.html" poster="../../week-13/sims/pivot-lab.png" title="Pivot Lab: summarize Rana's month" >}}

3. In **Pivot Lab**, choose Rows **Item** and Values **Count of sales**.
   Which items were sold four times?

   {{< record "Sold four times: …" >}}

   ::: {.check}
   **Pen, Juice and Notebook**: one sale in each of the four weeks. Count
   gives the number of sales, not the money.
   :::

   ::: {.choice}
   What does **Count of sales** give for each item?

   - [x] the number of its sales

     Why: Count counts the rows of each item.

   - [ ] the money of its sales

     Why: That is Sum of Total.

   - [ ] its average sale

     Why: That is Average of Total.
   :::

## Experiment 3 · The right chart and checked insights

**The idea:** compare categories: a **column chart**; a change over time:
a **line** (or columns in time order); the parts of one whole: a **pie**
(few parts). Give the chart a clear title. An **insight** is a short, true
sentence with a number. An AI tool can draft insights; check each one with
the PivotTable.

**Aim:** make the right chart, and write three checked insights.

::: {.part}
**Part A · In the apps (Excel and an AI assistant)**
:::

1. Click the PivotTable (Week in Rows) › **PivotTable Analyze ›
   PivotChart**. Choose the right chart for the boxes of each week › OK.
   Click the title of the chart and type a real title.

   {{< record "My chart … ; my title …" >}}

   ::: {.check}
   A **line chart** (or columns in week order): the weeks are a change
   over time. A real title, for example "Boxes taken per week". The line
   stays flat from week 1 to week 2 (10, 10), then goes up to 17.
   :::

   ::: {.choice}
   Which chart shows the boxes of each week?

   - [x] a line chart, in week order

     Why: The weeks are a change over time.

   - [ ] a pie chart

     Why: A pie shows the parts of one whole, not a change.

   - [ ] no chart: the table is enough

     Why: A chart shows the change at once.
   :::

2. Copy the table, without its total row. In the AI assistant, type
   *Write three short insights about these boxes of supplies, each with a
   number:* and paste it. Check each number with your PivotTables. Under
   the chart, write three checked insights and one line of AI-use
   statement.

   {{< record "A wrong or unclear AI insight … ; my best insight …" lines=2 >}}

   ::: {.check}
   Check each number: Paper 19, Gloves 12, Cups 6, total 37; weeks 10, 10
   and 17. A good insight: "Paper was the most used item, with 19 boxes."
   A good statement: "Insights drafted with an AI tool and checked with the
   PivotTables."
   :::

   ::: {.sort}
   Check each AI insight with the PivotTables. Sort them.

   Right: keep it
   :   Paper was the most used item, with 19 boxes.

       Why: Paper 19 is more than Gloves 12 and Cups 6.

   :   Week 3 used the most boxes, 17.

       Why: 17 is more than 10 and 10.

   Wrong: correct or delete it
   :   The store gave out 39 boxes in three weeks.

       Why: 39 counts the row typed twice; the clean total is 37.

   :   Gloves were used the most.

       Why: Gloves 12 is less than Paper 19.
   :::

::: {.part}
**Part B · On the simulator** (no computer? do it on your phone)
:::

{{< sim file="../../week-07/sims/chart-lab.html" poster="../../week-07/sims/chart-lab.png" title="Chart Lab: the right chart for the question" >}}

3. In **Chart Lab**, show the part of each type in the total of the week
   (185 JD). Which chart do you choose, and what part is Paper?

   {{< record "The chart … ; Paper …" >}}

   ::: {.check}
   **A pie chart**: it shows the parts of one whole. Paper is about **41
   %** (75 of 185 JD), Bags 32 % and Drinks 27 %.
   :::

   ::: {.choice}
   When is a pie chart the right chart?

   - [x] for the parts of one whole, with few parts

     Why: Each slice is one part of the total.

   - [ ] for a change over time

     Why: That is a line chart.

   - [ ] to compare twenty shops

     Why: Twenty slices are too many: use columns.
   :::
